{{Quote|Every galaxy has an underworld.|Official trailer|<ref name="Trailer">{{SWYouTube|rOJ1cw6mohw|The Book of Boba Fett | Official Trailer | Disney+|sw_url=video/official-trailer-the-book-of-boba-fett}}</ref>}}
'''''Star Wars: The Book of Boba Fett''''' is a live-action television series that focuses on the character [[Boba Fett]] taking place after the events of the [[The Mandalorian Season Two|second season]] of ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian|The Mandalorian]]'' but before the events of the [[The Mandalorian Season Three|third season]] of ''The Mandalorian''. Its first episode was released on [[December 29]], [[2021]]. It was first teased, with both its title and release window, in a post-credits sequence of the season two [[Chapter 16: The Rescue|finale]] of ''The Mandalorian''.

==Official description==
''The Book of Boba Fett, a thrilling Star Wars adventure, finds legendary bounty hunter Boba Fett and mercenary Fennec Shand navigating the galaxy's underworld when they return to the sands of Tatooine to stake their claim on the territory once ruled by Jabba the Hutt and his crime syndicate.''<ref name="Premiere date" />

==Development==
[[Boba Fett]] made his live-action return to ''Star Wars'' in ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]''{{'s}} "[[Chapter 14: The Tragedy]]," an episode directed by [[Robert Rodriguez]]. Series executive producer [[Jon Favreau]] originally approached Rodriguez to direct the important episode because he loved Rodriguez's interpretation of the character. He also decided to pitch to Rodriguez and the studio the idea of creating more episodes centering around the character. Although Rodriguez usually avoided franchises, that changed with Boba, as Rodriguez felt that he was an underdeveloped character and that it was as if he was an original character Rodriguez could expand.<ref name="THR">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/robert-rodriguez-interview-book-of-boba-fett-star-wars-1235062364|text=How 'The Book of Boba Fett' Will Shake Up 'Star Wars'|author=James Hibberd|date=2021-12-16|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20211216143038}}</ref>

[[File:TheBookOfBobaFett-TMCh6.png|thumb|left|300px|Following the end credits scene of ''The Mandalorian'' season two finale, the title was officially made known.]]
Reports of a Boba Fett–centered [[Disney+]] miniseries first surfaced online in early [[November]] [[2020]]. The reports also mentioned that the series' filming had begun.<ref name="Deadline">{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2020/11/the-mandalorian-season-3-production-start-date-spinoff-casting-disney-plus-sophie-thatcher-1234609860|text='The Mandalorian' Eyes Production Start As Spinoff, Casting & Boba Fett Buzz Heats Up|author=Nellie Andreeva|date=2020-01-05|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20201218210808}}</ref> On [[December 10]], 2020, [[Kathleen Kennedy]] teased that the "next chapter" of ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'' would arrive on [[December 24|Christmas]] of [[2021]].<ref name="Investor2020">{{DisneyCompany|url=disney-investor-day-2020|text=Disney Investor Day 2020}}</ref> Although many fans perceived this to be the [[The Mandalorian Season Three|third season]] of ''The Mandalorian'',<ref name="Fans1">{{WebCite|Date=2020-12-18|url=https://www.kvue.com/article/entertainment/entertainment-tonight/the-mandalorian-our-biggest-questions-after-the-season-2-finale/603-f13b182d-381f-4da6-836c-a51eb34e646e|text='The Mandalorian': Our Biggest Questions After the Season 2 Finale|author=John Bone|work=[[Wikipedia:KVUE|KVUE]]|archivedate=20201222030622|nolive=1}}</ref><ref name="Fans2">{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbr.com/disney-gallery-mandalorian-season-2-date|text=Disney Gallery: The Mandalorian Sets Season 2 Premiere Date|author=Sandy Schaefer|date=2020-12-16|work=[[Wikipedia:Comic Book Resources|''Comic Book Resources'']]|archivedate=20201222030948}}</ref> "[[Chapter 16: The Rescue]]," the [[The Mandalorian Season Two|Season Two]] finale of ''The Mandalorian'' released on [[December 18]], 2020, teased that ''The Book of Boba Fett'' would be the show to arrive in that timeframe instead.<ref name="Chapter 16">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}}</ref>

The following [[December 21|Monday]], show producer Jon Favreau appeared on ''Good Morning America'' on the [[ABC Television Network]]. He clarified that the two were separate shows, with ''The Book of Boba Fett'' arriving first.<ref name="GMA YouTube">{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@GMA|name=Good Morning America|link=Wikipedia:Good Morning America|video=uwwrezdcLiA|text=Jon Favreau talks about the season 2 finale of 'The Mandalorian'}}</ref> A [[StarWars.com]] post later that day reiterated this and stated that ''The Mandalorian'' Season Three would go into production in 2021.<ref name="Announcement" /> Filming officially wrapped on [[June 8]], 2021,<ref name="Wrap">{{WebCite|url=https://movieweb.com/the-book-of-boba-fett-wraps-production|text=The Book of Boba Fett Wraps Filming Season One|author=Jeremy Dick|date=2021-06-08|work=[[Wikipedia:MovieWeb|MovieWeb]]|archivedate=20210608191908}}</ref> and the series was still in post-production as of [[September]] of that year.<ref name="i205">{{InsiderCite|205|Launchpad}}</ref>

===Music===
On [[September 22]], [[2021]], it was reported that [[Ludwig Göransson]] would be composing the music for the show.<ref name="Composer">{{WebCite|url=http://filmmusicreporter.com/2021/09/22/ludwig-goransson-scoring-disneys-the-book-of-boba-fett|text=Ludwig Göransson Scoring Disney+'s 'The Book of Boba Fett'|date=2021-09-23|work=[http://filmmusicreporter.com Film Music Reporter]|archivedate=20210922101821}}</ref> The show is scored by [[Joseph Shirley]], while Göransson composed the music themes, including the title theme.<ref name="Chapter 1" /> [[The Book of Boba Fett: Vol. 1 (Chapters 1-4) (Original Soundtrack)|The soundtrack of the first four episodes]] was released digitally on [[January 21]], [[2022]].<ref name="soundtrack vol1">{{Apple|subdomain=music|url=nz/album/the-book-of-boba-fett-vol-1-chapters-1-4-original-soundtrack/1606018530|text=The Book of Boba Fett: Vol. 1 (Chapters 1-4)}}</ref> [[The Book of Boba Fett: Vol. 2 (Chapters 5-7) (Original Soundtrack)|The soundtrack of the last three episodes]] was released digitally on [[February 11]], 2022.<ref name="soundtrack vol2">{{Apple|subdomain=music|url=nz/album/the-book-of-boba-fett-vol-2-chapters-5-7-original-soundtrack/1609288653|text=The Book of Boba Fett: Vol. 2 (Chapters 5-7)}}</ref>

All the parts of the main title theme were sung by Göransson himself. The theme was inspired by Björn Isfält's score to the Swedish 1984 movie ''Ronja Rövardotter''.<ref name="Sveriges Radio">{{WebCite|url=https://sverigesradio.se/artikel/rovarsangen-som-inspirerade-till-musiken-i-tv-serien-boba-fett|text=Rövarsången som inspirerade till musiken i tv-serien Boba Fett?|date=2022-01-17|work=[[Wikipedia:Sveriges Radio|Sveriges Radio]]|language=Swedish|archivedate=20220528000708}}</ref>

==Release and reception==
===Trailers===
The first teaser trailer was released on [[November 1]], [[2021]].<ref name="Trailer" /> The promotional trailers mainly used the first minutes of the series premiere as, according to Rodriguez, the second half of the episode gave too much information.<ref name="THR" /><ref name="Chapter 1" />

==Adaptations and tie-in media==
''[[Disney Gallery: The Book of Boba Fett]]'', a special which focused on behind-the-scenes aspects of ''The Book of Boba Fett'', premiered on [[May 4]], 2022.<ref name="D23 May 2022">{{D23|url=everything-new-you-can-stream-on-disney-in-may-2022|text=Everything New You Can Stream on Disney+ in May 2022}}</ref>
